expect: An abandoned Odin/Plesk hosting control panel still answering on 443 with a self-signed 1024-bit RSA certificate issued for a completely different name. OpenSSL 3 rejects the key as too weak before it ever reaches the name or the dates, so the crawler must record a TLS failure rather than retry or store an empty page.
evidence: measured 2026-07-27, two httpx GETs ~6s apart, identical class: probe1 2.1s -> ConnectError('[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: EE certificate key too weak (_ssl.c:1006)') ; probe2 0.6s -> ConnectError('[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: EE certificate key too weak (_ssl.c:1006)') (httpx timeout budget 8s, verify=True, follow_redirects=False). Leaf pulled separately with verification disabled to explain the failure: TLSv1.2 / DHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, 665-byte DER, subject == issuer (self-signed) 'emailAddress=webmaster@odin.com,CN=odin.com,OU=Odin Automation,O=Odin,L=Moscow,ST=Moscow,C=RU', RSA key size 1024, sigalg sha256, notBefore 2016-03-22 notAfter 2036-03-17, no subjectAltName extension at all.

expect: A live municipal police portal fronted by an old appliance that only offers unsafe legacy renegotiation. The handshake itself fails, so no certificate is ever presented and there is nothing to fall back on - the crawler must bucket this as a TLS error, not as an empty or slow page.
evidence: measured 2026-07-27, two httpx GETs ~6s apart, identical class: probe1 1.2s -> ConnectError('[SSL: UNSAFE_LEGACY_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED] unsafe legacy renegotiation disabled (_ssl.c:1006)') ; probe2 0.3s -> ConnectError('[SSL: UNSAFE_LEGACY_RENEGOTIATION_DISABLED] unsafe legacy renegotiation disabled (_ssl.c:1006)') (httpx timeout budget 8s, verify=True, follow_redirects=False). Distinct from every certificate-validation case in this corpus: a follow-up raw ssl socket with check_hostname=False and verify_mode=CERT_NONE ALSO failed with the same SSLError, i.e. the failure is in the handshake and not in path validation, so no leaf certificate could be retrieved at all.

expect: The US Defense Technical Information Center serves a perfectly current certificate that simply chains to the DoD PKI, which is in no public trust store. Dates are valid and the hostname matches, so this is a pure untrusted-root failure - the case most likely to be mistaken for a site being down when a defence crawler meets it.
evidence: measured 2026-07-27, two httpx GETs ~6s apart, identical class: probe1 1.5s -> ConnectError('[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1006)') ; probe2 0.2s -> ConnectError('[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1006)') (httpx timeout budget 8s, verify=True, follow_redirects=False). Leaf pulled separately with verification disabled to explain the failure: TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384, 1540-byte DER, subject 'CN=com-apps-dtic.cce.af.mil,OU=USAF,OU=PKI,OU=DoD,O=U.S. Government,C=US', issuer 'CN=DOD SW CA-82,OU=PKI,OU=DoD,O=U.S. Government,C=US', RSA 2048 sha256, notBefore 2026-05-15 notAfter 2027-06-16 (in date), SAN includes 'dtic.mil' and '*.dtic.mil' (hostname matches). The only defect is the private DoD issuing CA.

expect: Skimlinks' production affiliate redirector go.redirectingat.com takes its next destination in a ?url= query parameter and will happily forward to itself. Stacked 25 deep it burns a 30x on every hop without ever reaching content. Unlike the httpbin counters elsewhere in this corpus this is a redirector a crawler actually meets in the wild, on any monetised page, so the hop cap has to hold on real hosts and not just on test endpoints.
evidence: Live manual redirect walk 2026-07-27 (httpx, follow_redirects=False, one hop at a time, cookies persisted, 12-hop budget): sanity check first - a single un-nested https://go.redirectingat.com/?url=<target> returns one 302 straight to the target. The same redirector nested 25 deep (URL length 4670 chars) returned 302 on hop1, hop2, hop3, hop4, hop5, hop6, hop7, hop8, hop9, hop10, hop11 and hop12 - twelve consecutive 30x, no 2xx at any point - and the budget was EXHAUSTED with the walker still sitting on a 30x at https://go.redirectingat.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2F, i.e. one more redirect still owed. Depth is load-bearing and was measured: 23 and 24 levels also exhaust the 12-hop budget, while 26 levels and deeper are rejected by the edge with a single HTTP 502 (URL too long) instead of redirecting.
